text:
kevin: quick idea — add an optional `X-Embed-Dims` header from clients so router can prefer dim-optimized shards. keeps payloads intact, no client-side splitting required. thoughts? :thinking_face:
maria: curious — what's the goal vs current preflight/dim-splitting flow?
kevin: currently router guesses dims from payload length or preflight, then splitter may split or fail. this header would be an explicit hint so we can route to 1536/2048-capable nodes and avoid wasting split capacity.
olivia: love the intent, worried about quota accounting. if we route bigger-dim requests to special pool, do they consume different quotas? customers will ask.
jiang: +1 on planning for quotas. propose: header used only for routing; billing remains per-token/embedding. but console needs new telemetry to show dim distribution per-customer.
samir: small UX note — SDKs would need to surface this header. prefer auto-populate from embedding vector length on client side; fallback to header if set.
kevin: yeah SDK auto-populate sounds ideal, but we can't force it. header as escape hatch for advanced customers.
maria: technically how would router verify the header? we should validate against actual payload dims to avoid spoofing. malicious header could route heavy jobs into small pools.
jiang: validation rule: if header present, compute dim from incoming shape and compare; if mismatch > 1% then log + drop header (route conservative). add metric `embed.dim_header_mismatch` and alert on spikes.
console-bot: new dashboard widget available in staging: "Embed dim heatmap" (per-model, per-customer). shows p50/p95 latency per dim bucket :bar_chart:
olivia: nice, can we show routed-pool attribution too? want to triage perf regressions (is slowness because wrong pool or kv-cache misses).
kevin: yes, add `routed_pool` tag to traces/spans and to the heatmap drilldown. also surface fallback rate when pool capacity is exhausted.
samir: rollout plan: 1) accept header + validate (no routing change), 2) enable routing in canary to dim-optimized pool for internal tenants, 3) SDK auto-populate release, 4) public rollout with console toggle.
maria: agree. add a soft-quota on dim-pool to avoid noisy-customer jank — throttle and fallback to general pool with backoff. log throttles to `embed.dim_pool_throttle` metric.
jiang: telemetry asks: we need histograms of batch sizes, token counts, and kv-cache hit rate per-dim. Also capture percentile of sequence lengths by dim bucket. I'll add to tracing schema.
kevin: example header/curl (for SDK teams):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -H "X-Embed-Dims: 1536" \n  -d '{"model":"open-embedding-xl","input":["foo","bar"]}'
```
olivia: re: console UI — let's add a toggle in model rollout page: "Prefer dim-optimized routing" with canary % and show estimated cost delta and latency impact. product will love the numbers.
samir: do we need migration docs for Dedicated customers? some on-prem/private may not have dim pools. fallback behavior must be explicit.
maria: yes docs + server-side feature flag. default: header ignored if no dim pool. mustn't 413.
kevin: last: security — ensure header not used for privilege escalation (no routing to higher-tier nodes unless customer authorized). add authorization check: `customer.allowed_dim_pools` claim.
deploy-bot: deploy queued: router-validate-header v2 -> staging at 2851234578 by ci/cd :rocket:
kevin: i'll watch staging telemetry later and loop back with a short runbook for SRE on how to rollback. :+1:
